articles.intro: No. Bread, rice, potatoes and pasta can fit into weight management. Portions and the whole eating pattern matter more than banning carbohydrates.
sections: Choose what works on your plate

Higher-fibre versions can be useful, but they are not a licence for unlimited portions. Notice what comes with the carbohydrate: a baked potato and a plate of chips are different meals. A medically prescribed diet needs individual advice.
What you can do next
Try a normal portion of rice, potatoes or bread alongside vegetables and a protein food. Change one meal you repeat rather than removing an entire food group.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/nutrition-guide

articles.intro: No. Your diet needs some fat. Fat is energy dense, so both the kind and the amount deserve attention.
sections: A useful swap

Replacing some saturated fat with unsaturated fat is different from simply adding oil, nuts or avocado to everything. Foods described as healthy still contribute energy. A low-fat label also says little about the rest of a product.
What you can do next
Compare two foods you regularly buy. Look at saturated fat and the portion you actually eat, then make a manageable swap.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/nutrition-guide

articles.intro: Breakfast is not compulsory for weight loss. The useful question is whether your eating pattern leaves you nourished and able to manage the rest of your day.
sections: Make the decision from your day

If skipping breakfast means you arrive ravenous at lunch, try an easy breakfast. If eating early feels uncomfortable, plan a later meal instead. Avoid using a missed meal as punishment. Diabetes medicines or another medical condition may make meal timing important.
What you can do next
Compare a few ordinary workdays. Keep the breakfast or later-meal option that helps you eat regularly without a scramble. Ask your clinician about timing if treatment affects it.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/nutrition-guide

articles.intro: Yes. A takeaway can fit into a weight-management plan. Frequency, portion size, drinks and extras all affect the overall meal.
sections: Decide before you order

Choose the part you most want and question the automatic extras. A main meal with a suitable side may suit you better than a bundle you would not otherwise buy. A single takeaway does not need a compensatory fast the next day.
What you can do next
Pick your order before you are very hungry. Keep the next meal ordinary and return to your usual routine.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/healthy-takeaways-men

articles.intro: Yes. You can enjoy a barbecue while working on your weight. Choose a satisfying plate and pay attention to food safety.
sections: Build a meal, not a ban

Try a main protein food, vegetables or salad, and the bread or potatoes you enjoy. Sauces, grazing and drinks can turn a meal into much more than you intended. Keep raw and cooked foods separate and follow safe cooking instructions.
What you can do next
Decide what you want on your plate, then sit down and enjoy it. Use the barbecue guide for meal ideas and the linked food-safety advice.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/healthy-bbq-men

articles.intro: There is no single protein target that fits every man. Body size, activity, age and medical needs can change what is appropriate.
sections: Start with ordinary food

Include protein foods across meals, such as beans, eggs, fish, dairy or suitable alternatives. A calculator gives a planning estimate, not a clinical prescription. Kidney disease, poor intake or other nutritional concerns need individual advice. Supplements are not automatically necessary.
What you can do next
Look at your usual breakfast, lunch and dinner. Find the meal that is missing a practical protein option. Ask a dietitian if you need a personal target.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/tools/protein

articles.intro: Alcohol contributes energy, but it does not explain every change around your waist. Drinking can also affect the food choices you make around it.
sections: Count the whole occasion

Mixers, late food and the next-day routine can matter as well as the drink. A smaller waist is not the only reason to review alcohol. If you may be dependent, get medical advice before suddenly stopping.
What you can do next
Record an ordinary week honestly, including serving sizes. Choose one realistic change, such as fewer drinking occasions or an alcohol-free option you enjoy.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/weight-and-blood-pressure-men

articles.intro: Stress can change eating, sleep, drinking and activity. It can contribute to weight change, but it is not a diagnosis or a complete explanation.
sections: Notice the pattern without blaming yourself

Perhaps lunch disappears during busy shifts, food becomes comfort at night, or sleep is repeatedly interrupted. Those are useful clues. Unexplained weight change or persistent symptoms deserve a health assessment rather than an online cortisol label.
What you can do next
Identify the hardest part of the day and make one practical adjustment. Speak to a GP if stress is hard to cope with or self-help is not helping.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/mental-health

articles.intro: Sleep can affect how manageable food, movement and daily routines feel. Improving sleep is worthwhile even when the scale does not immediately change.
sections: Treat the sleep problem itself

Do not assume tiredness is just your weight or a lack of willpower. Persistent insomnia, loud snoring with breathing pauses, or marked daytime sleepiness can need assessment. A sleep routine is a starting point, not a substitute for that assessment.
What you can do next
Choose a consistent waking time and a workable wind-down. If sleep problems persist or affect daily life, speak to a GP.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/sleep-stress-mindset-emotional-eating-maintenance

articles.intro: Yes. Walking is a practical way to increase activity, though the amount of weight change varies. It can benefit your routine and fitness even without rapid weight loss.
sections: Start from your current ability

You do not need to begin with a step target copied from somebody else. A short walk that you repeat can be more useful than an exhausting first outing. Increase time or pace gradually and get advice if symptoms or a condition make activity difficult.
What you can do next
Choose a short, familiar route and a time you can repeat. Use how comfortable it feels to decide whether to add a little more.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/beginner-walking-plan-men

articles.intro: No. A gym is one option. Walking, home exercise and everyday movement can be part of a useful plan.
sections: Make access easy

Equipment and memberships do not make a routine automatically sustainable. Choose something that fits your time, budget and ability. Strength work can be done at home with suitable exercises; it need not start with heavy weights.
What you can do next
Pick one convenient movement option and put it into a normal day. If you want strength work, start with the beginner home guide.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/home-strength-men

articles.intro: A daily scale change is not a direct measurement of fat gained or lost. Water, food and bowel contents, timing and other factors can move the number.
sections: Compare like with like

Use similar weighing conditions and look at several readings over time. A single number is poor evidence for changing everything. Unexpected rapid change, swelling or other symptoms should be discussed with a clinician.
What you can do next
Keep the next meal and activity ordinary. If you track weight, record the reading without turning it into a verdict on the day.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/member/progress

articles.intro: Choose a frequency that gives you useful information without making weight the centre of every day. There is no compulsory weighing schedule.
sections: The conditions matter too

Using the same scales at a similar time helps comparison. Repeated readings are more informative than one isolated result. If weighing worsens anxiety, distress or eating difficulties, another way to monitor progress may be more appropriate.
What you can do next
Agree a manageable schedule for yourself or with your clinician. Also notice strength, walking comfort, sleep and other goals that matter to you.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/member/progress

articles.intro: There is no personal weekly rate this page can prescribe. Starting weight, health, food intake and treatment all affect what is appropriate.
sections: Avoid a deadline that drives poor intake

Faster change is not automatically better. A target should leave room for nutrition, strength and daily functioning. Specialist diets and prescribed treatment need their own monitoring. Unexpected or unintentional loss needs assessment.
What you can do next
Choose sustainable changes and discuss your personal target with a qualified professional if health or treatment is involved. Review the trend rather than forcing a weekly result.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/mens-weight-management-guide

articles.intro: Carrying more fat around the waist can be associated with greater cardiometabolic risk. A waist measurement is a clue, not a diagnosis.
sections: Look beyond appearance

Blood pressure, blood tests, family history and other findings can matter. You cannot identify visceral fat precisely from a photograph or decide that someone is healthy by their shape. Waist-to-height ratio can add context to BMI in appropriate adults.
What you can do next
Measure consistently if that is useful to you. Ask about relevant health checks instead of choosing treatment from waist size alone.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/health-mot

articles.intro: Losing excess weight can contribute to lower blood pressure for some people. It does not guarantee a normal reading or replace prescribed treatment.
sections: Measure the outcome

Blood pressure has several influences, and a diagnosis depends on proper measurement and assessment. Do not reduce or stop blood-pressure medicine because your weight has changed. Your clinician can review readings and symptoms together.
What you can do next
Arrange a blood-pressure check or follow your agreed home-monitoring plan. Take the readings to a review rather than judging treatment from the scales.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/weight-and-blood-pressure-men

articles.intro: Changes in weight, food and activity may improve cholesterol for some people. The result needs to be checked with a blood test.
sections: Weight is not the whole explanation

Inherited conditions and other health factors can affect cholesterol. Reducing saturated fat may be useful, but diet changes do not make prescribed medicine automatically unnecessary. A smaller waist cannot tell you your cholesterol level.
What you can do next
Ask when your cholesterol should next be checked and what the different results mean for you. Keep medication changes with the clinician managing them.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/cholesterol-men

articles.intro: For people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes, suitable lifestyle changes and weight management can reduce risk. They do not provide a guarantee.
sections: First find out your situation

A risk questionnaire cannot confirm whether you have diabetes. Blood testing and clinical assessment may be needed. Prevention is also different from managing established diabetes, where treatment and monitoring need an agreed plan.
What you can do next
Ask your GP about assessment and local prevention support. The NHS England programme is one route for eligible people in England; arrangements vary across the UK.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/articles/prediabetes-men

articles.intro: A 20% reduction is not realistic or appropriate for everyone. It is a large milestone, not the definition of successful weight management.
sections: Trial averages are not your target

A medicine study describes a particular group under particular conditions. It cannot promise your result. Smaller changes and better health measures can be meaningful, and maintaining weight can also be an appropriate goal.
What you can do next
Choose goals that reflect your health and circumstances. Discuss a personal weight target with your clinician where treatment is involved.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/faq/what-is-20-percent-club

articles.intro: The 20% Club describes a milestone of losing one fifth of starting body weight. It is not a treatment target everybody needs to reach.
sections: Understand the arithmetic

For a starting weight of 100 kg, 20% is 20 kg. That calculation says nothing by itself about the safest route, the time needed or whether the target suits you. Progress and health are broader than membership of a named milestone.
What you can do next
Use the percentage calculator for context. Pick a suitable goal without making a badge the reason to over-restrict food or change a prescription.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/my-target

articles.intro: Yes. Mounjaro can be prescribed to eligible adult men when a qualified prescriber finds it appropriate. Being male does not by itself qualify or disqualify you.
sections: An assessment is still needed

Tirzepatide has specific licensed uses, suitability criteria, warnings and interactions. Diabetes treatment and weight-management prescribing are different questions. Eligibility, supply and follow-up must be assessed; the medicine should not be borrowed or bought from an unverified seller.
What you can do next
Discuss your health history and current medicines with a qualified prescriber. SHIFT does not currently prescribe or supply Mounjaro.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/glp1-guide

articles.intro: Yes. Eligible adult men can be prescribed Wegovy after appropriate assessment. It is not a treatment reserved for women.
sections: The product and route matter

Semaglutide products and formulations have distinct prescribing instructions. A BMI calculator or online article cannot decide suitability, choose a dose or authorise a switch. Availability through a service is separate from a medicine having UK authorisation.
What you can do next
Ask the prescriber which formulation and care pathway they are discussing. SHIFT does not currently prescribe or supply Wegovy.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/glp1-guide

articles.intro: No. GLP-1 and related weight-management medicines can be prescribed to eligible adult men. Suitability depends on the person and the particular product.
sections: Avoid treating them as one interchangeable medicine
Licensed uses, formulations, contraindications and instructions differ. A friend’s prescription or dose is not a starting point for your treatment. Your own history and current medicines need review.
What you can do next
Use the treatment guides to prepare questions, then speak to a qualified prescriber. SHIFT cannot establish eligibility or supply a prescription through this FAQ.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/treatments

articles.intro: No. Mounjaro contains tirzepatide; Ozempic contains semaglutide. They are different medicines and are not interchangeable dose for dose.
sections: Check the purpose as well as the name

Ozempic is a diabetes product. Mounjaro has diabetes and adult weight-management uses under specific criteria. A comparison of ingredient names does not establish which medicine, if any, is appropriate for you.
What you can do next
Take the exact product name, formulation and current prescription to your clinician. Do not combine or switch products yourself.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/treatments

articles.intro: Wegovy and Ozempic both contain semaglutide, but they are distinct products. Their licensed uses and prescribing instructions differ.
sections: Do not infer a substitute from the ingredient

Ozempic is a diabetes product. Wegovy is used for weight management under its own criteria and now has different UK-authorised formulations. A supply problem does not make a self-directed brand or formulation switch safe.
What you can do next
Ask your prescriber about the exact product and current care plan. Follow its own leaflet and keep changes with that prescriber.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/guides/glp1-guide

articles.intro: No. SHIFT does not currently prescribe or supply medicines. Information pages and My Timber support do not create a clinical prescribing service.
sections: Keep treatment decisions with your care team

A medicine catalogue is information about products, not an offer to supply them. Ordering remains closed while a regulated clinical partner and the required care arrangements are uncommissioned. Coaching cannot authorise eligibility, a dose change or a prescription.
What you can do next
Speak to your GP or an appropriately qualified prescriber about treatment. Use SHIFT to organise practical food, movement and day-to-day questions.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/clinical-governance

articles.intro: No. SHIFT is not a replacement for your GP, emergency care or an individual medical assessment.
sections: Use each service for its purpose

My Timber can support ordinary planning and reflection. Public tools can help organise questions. They cannot examine you, order diagnostic tests, prescribe treatment or decide that worrying symptoms are safe. AI responses also need to stay within these limits.
What you can do next
Take symptoms and treatment questions to an appropriate healthcare professional. For urgent or severe symptoms, use the relevant urgent-care service rather than waiting for an app response.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/medical-disclaimer

articles.intro: No. The public Health MOT is an informational self-check. It does not diagnose a condition or establish treatment eligibility.
sections: Its outputs are prompts

Some inputs use established measurement thresholds; others describe routines or reported symptoms. A priority label is a reason to look more closely, not a clinical finding. The tool has not established your personal risk of a heart attack or which medicine you should take.
What you can do next
Print or save the report if it helps you prepare questions for an appointment. Take worrying symptoms to a clinician regardless of the tool’s output.
sources: SHIFT: Health MOT methodology and limitations
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/health-mot

articles.intro: Yes. The public Health MOT saves its answers and report data in this browser’s local storage on this device. It does not upload them into your My Timber account.
sections: A shared device needs care

The saved profile can remain after closing the page and may be visible to somebody using the same browser. Clearing this site’s browser data removes the local copy. Account-backed health information is separate and has its own privacy controls; clearing browser data does not erase that account data.
What you can do next
Use a private device for sensitive answers. Print or save the report only where you want a copy, and review the privacy page for account-backed information.
sources: SHIFT: Health MOT methodology and limitations
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/health-mot-methodology

articles.intro: Women can use public tools where the tool’s stated scope fits. SHIFT’s main audience is adult men, so check the assumptions before using a result.
sections: Not every calculator fits every situation

A result based on a male default, adult thresholds or a general planning formula may not be appropriate for you. Pregnancy, an eating disorder, childhood and certain medical conditions can require a different assessment. A calculator is not personal medical advice.
What you can do next
Read the tool’s inputs and limitations. Choose individual professional advice when your circumstances sit outside them.
sources: SHIFT: Health MOT methodology and limitations
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/tools

articles.intro: A Founding Shifter is someone who registers interest in SHIFT and its updates. It does not mean you have bought membership or secured treatment.
sections: Check what the current route offers

The Founding Members page describes the available registration route and what follows. Future invitations or offers should be read when actually announced. The label does not promise medication, final pricing or a place ahead of someone with greater clinical need.
What you can do next
Use the registration method shown on the current Founding Members page. My Timber access and a mailing-list registration are separate choices.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/founding-members

articles.intro: The Timber Mill is SHIFT’s planned clothing and gear range. The current shop is a preview; ordering and checkout are not available.
sections: Concepts are not available stock

A preview image or a description of a future reward does not mean an item can be bought or claimed today. Availability, prices and any reward terms need to be published when the relevant product or programme is ready.
What you can do next
Explore the current shop page for what is actually shown. Use a displayed interest route if you want to contribute feedback on the planned range.
next: Explore the relevant guide or tool
/shop
